decisions.reason: As an extension of the firm's established training and support business that remained visible beyond launch, it likely meets aspiration levels well enough and is cheap to carry within the firm's available slack.

This accessory builds directly on the installed machine base and modular engineering capabilities, so even with limited evidence after launch it is likely satisfactory enough to retain as a complementary offer.

Because it is distant from the firm's established offer, its fit, sales learning, and support economics are more uncertain, making it the clearest candidate for problemistic search and resource reallocation if results fall short of aspiration.
A high-speed CNC milling machine is close to the firm's core business and strategic direction, so management would usually keep it unless performance clearly disappointed relative to aspirations.
The automatic tool change system fits the firm's productivity-oriented machinery portfolio and should benefit from cross-selling and existing know-how, reducing the likelihood of withdrawal.
